newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end broadly lower, Dow falls 59 points.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end broadly lower, Dow falls 59 points.

text.p: Wall Street stocks suffered broad losses on Friday, as mounting interest rate pressure and increasing concern about the market's near-term outlook sent the Dow industrials to their third consecutive decline.
The Dow fell 59 points to end the week at an unofficial 6696, down nearly 200 points from their record close of 6883.90 on Tuesday.
Broader indicators mirrored the Dow's decline and a number of analysts said the retreat by stocks was looking more and more like the start of a corrective phase for the market.
Equity investors also grew more concerned about interest rates, which edged still higher as the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treausry fell 13/32, pushing the yield up to 6.89 percent.

"The bond market is about five percent off its high, and for the stock market to decline about five percent off its high would not be out of the realm of the possible," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co.
In contrast with Thursday, when stocks met with a sudden and sharp wave of program selling at the end of the day, the Friday session was marked by sweeping advances and declines.
Several times during the session, buy programs lifted the Dow up from its lows, as fund managers put to work the vast amounts of retirement account cash at their disposal.
"People still bought the dip," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The deployment of funds continues."
But even as the fund money was providing something of a safety net for stocks, some analysts were mulling aloud the prudence of buying at these near-record levels, even on dips.
"This is very different because for the first time in the last five years, the market has become overvalued," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
Johnson said based on an analysis of corporate earnings and price-to-earnings ratios, the market had reached a level where substantial further gains would be hard to come by.
Hit hardest by the session's downdraft were financial and transportation stocks, which are particularly sensitive to fluctuations in interest rates.
Among major banks, Citicorp slid 3-3/8 to 109-3/8, BankAmerica Corp fell 3-1/8 to 105-1/2 and Chase Manhattan Corp shed two to 89-1/8.
American Airlines parent AMR Corp fell 1-1/8 to 84-7/8 and Delta Air Lines Inc dipped 1-1/4 to 81-1/8.
Many technology stocks also suffered losses, pulling the Nasdaq Composite down by 14.54 points to 1363.83.
Leading the decline was Cascade Communications Corp, which plummeted 23-1/8, or 36 percent, to 41 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings late Thursday.

Even though Cascade's earnings rose sharply and were in line with Wall Street estimates, analysts focused on signs of weaker growth ahead, such as the company's slower collections of accounts receivable.
The concern spilled over to other networking equipment shares. Cisco Systems Inc fell 3-1/8 to 68-5/8, and NYSE-listed shares in Canada-based Newbridge Networks Corp fell 1-1/2 to 32-5/8.
The Dow's loss brought its decline for the week to 136.62 points, the first full week this year in which it lost ground.
The S&P 500 index fell 7.04 to 770.52, leaving that index 5.65 points lower for the week.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
